title: Prefill-Aware Kernel Co-placement and Microblock Consolidation for Mixed-Workload Paged KV
creator: Emily Zhang
description: Goal: Reduce KV cache fragmentation and cross-kernel inefficiencies for mixed-sequence workloads by introducing microblock consolidation (compact adjacent small KV allocations into coalesced microblocks) and a prefill-aware kernel co-placement policy. This work targets paged attention + KV cache management: allocation, eviction, fragmentation, and reuse, with integration into kernel selection and prefill/decode scheduling so runtime chooses kernels that minimize KV movement and maximize cache reuse.
background: We observe high fragmentation in KV pages when serving mixed short- and long-context traffic concurrently (chat agents + batch completions). Fragmentation increases eviction churn, causing repeated prefill work and higher tail latency. Existing approaches in other tickets focused on page reclamation and slab compaction; however, those operate post-facto and do not coordinate with kernel selection or the prefill scheduler. This ticket combines allocation-time strategies (microblocks), an eviction scoring heuristic that factors prefill probability, and kernel co-placement hints to reduce cross-kernel cache thrash.
proposal: 1) Microblock allocator: divide KV pages into microblocks (e.g., 4-16 contiguous slots) tracked by a compact bitmap. New allocations try to pack same-request KV segments into the same microblock to improve locality and make coalescing cheaper. 2) Prefill probability estimator: lightweight model using recent sequence-length distribution, request prefix hashes, and recency to compute a per-request prefill score. 3) Eviction scoring: combine age, recency, frequency, and prefill_score into a single numeric rank used by the page/microblock eviction policy; penalize microblocks that are hot for imminent prefill. 4) Kernel co-placement hints: when selecting an attention kernel variant for prefill/decode (fast single-stream vs batched fused), propagate a hint that indicates preferred KV microblock placement (same GPU, same NUMA domain) and acceptable coalescing budget. 5) Prefill scheduler changes: prefer scheduling prefill tasks to devices that already host relevant microblocks or where co-location will be cheap; when that's not possible, consider lightweight prefill delta fetch (only missing microblocks) instead of full prefill.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (spike): implement microblock metadata and allocator on a single serving shard; expose metrics (microblock_fill_ratio, microblock_eviction_count). Implement simple prefill_score heuristic (LRU recency + sequence_length_probability). Phase 2: integrate eviction scoring and add kernel hint API to runtime. Phase 3: extend prefill scheduler to use hints and perform co-placement decisions; run load tests. Phase 4: gradual rollout with feature flag and compare with control using canary rollout. Rollback plan: revert kernel hinting and allocator changes independently if perf regressions occur.
acceptance_criteria:
- 15-25% reduction in microblock eviction churn in mixed workload benchmark (chat + batch completions).
- No more than 3% regression in mean latency; tail latency (p99) decreases by >= 5ms on mixed workloads.
- KV cache hit rate improves by >= 8% for targeted customers in canary group.
- Metrics and dashboards added: microblock_fill_ratio, prefill_score_distribution, eviction_rank_distribution, co-placement_ratio.

Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec per GPU, KV eviction rate, microblock fill ratio, additional memory overhead
Target machines: A100-80GB and RTX6000 configs in staging
design_tradeoffs: Microblock metadata increases per-page bookkeeping (bitmap and allocation index) -> overhead vs fragmentation reduction. We cap microblocks per page to keep metadata < 1% page size.

Aggressive co-placement may reduce throughput if it prevents optimal kernel batching across requests. We prioritize kernel batching when prefill_score is low; only enforce co-placement for high prefill_score requests.
Eviction scoring that favors prefill candidates may increase memory pressure for cold long-context requests; use soft thresholds and dynamic decay to avoid pathological retention.
Kernel hinting requires interface changes; keep hints advisory to maintain compatibility with legacy scheduling paths.
risks: Unexpected latency regressions when allocator introduces lock contention; mitigate with per-shard lock-free free-lists for microblocks.
Prefill_score misestimation could cause unnecessary retention; add adaptive calibration and fallback to frequency-based eviction.
Complexity increases operational debugging; add trace spans for allocation/coalescing decisions and logging knobs.
Interactions with dedicated tenants that pin GPUs may limit co-placement opportunities; include tenant-aware fallback policies.
qa_plan:
- Unit tests for microblock allocator and eviction ranker.
- Integration tests with runtime kernel hint path simulated.
- Staging soak test with synthetic mixed traffic for 72 hours.
- Canary metrics monitored for 48 hours with automated rollback on >=5% regression in p99 or >=10% increase in eviction rate.
notes: Spike found microblock_size=8 strikes best balance for our 32KB pages: reduces fragmentation 18% vs baseline with 0.8% metadata overhead.
Initial prefill_score uses exponential moving average of sequence length by prefix hash + last_seen_timestamp; we will evaluate adding a small ML model later.
